reasons.reader_question: Clear and specific: will she tell him before the cleft, and what is written beneath the Cairn? The ending's irony sharpens it.
reasons.change: Knowledge shifts hard: she learns Harish's fate and Udai's part. Her neutral-surveyor self-image breaks. Power shifts to the holder of the letter.
reasons.romance_movement: First costed kiss, then a new barrier: an oath plus an accusation against his grandfather. He offers the way anyway, so the reason is fresh.
reasons.shown_chemistry: Laugh against his mouth, careful hands on her face, hands held shaped in the air, open palm on snow. All responsive, little narration.
reasons.character_logic: Ila's silence is reasoned (oath, unknown guilt, queen's line). Kunal reading her hands openly fits his growth. The pre-reading kiss is motivated.
reasons.stakes_and_cost: Silence is free under the rope, and she hates that it is free. It costs him trust, and she sees the cost cross his face.
reasons.prose: Stacked 'a man who' similes, 'handed' echoed, some on-the-nose thesis lines, 'could not help looking' near-tell, and an overwrought mountain image.
reasons.continuity: F593 says she read the gloves' meaning by a hut fire, but this is an open shore shelf. The drawer's 'thirty winters' sits loosely against F619's 31-winter reign.

fixes: Continuity: the reading happens on 'a flat shelf, dry and out of the wind', but F593 says she read the gloves by a hut fire. The beat sets the shore, so revise F593 to the rock shelf above the Drum. Change 'I have kept that drawer thirty winters' to 'since my crowning' to match F619. Drop 'Ila's father found him' from new-facts, since the page never says it.

Prose: 'as if he had been handed something he had stopped expecting' echoes 'handed a riddle' three lines up. It joins a stack of 'a man who' similes (doorway, riddle, made himself wait, sleeping child). Keep two at most. Replace 'It was the size of a mountain, what he set down there' with one concrete beat of his hand on the snow. Change 'She looked, because she could not help looking' to 'She looked at his hands.'

Clarity: 'Every crosser a warden had hanged since. Meera's mother.' implies Meera's mother was hanged; write 'Meera's mother, dead of the cough behind the closed pass.' Cut the thesis line 'His closed hand was a hand over a grave.' The previous line already lands it. In the last line, 'tied the stitches shut' has no stitches to tie; write 'buttoned it inside her coat'.
reader_question: Will Ila tell Kunal that his grandfather walked hers to his death before he leads her down that same way, and what price is written beneath the Shilak Cairn?
new_facts_assessment: Udai coming home alive is needed and fits F635 and F526. The page never says Ila's father found Harish, so strike that clause from the fact. Sarala keeping the drawer thirty winters conflicts mildly with F619's thirty-one-winter reign; reword it. Making the archive oath separate from the nineteen-year-old surveyor's oath is needed, and it fits F553 and F639.
